a: Dogfood finding (2026-08-20, DOGFOOD-FINDINGS.md): 92 of 100 concepts in the lambo-dev store carry no durable embedding — interleaved in time, not one outage window; all 44 record_action Resources plus most Constraints/Logics/Entities. Semantic recall and dedup are blind to them and the damage is cumulative with no backfill path. Candidate product work: embedding-coverage counter in lambo_stats, and a re-embed backfill verb. Cause unsettled: record_action-never-embeds by design, intermittent embedder unavailability degrading hybrid to keyword, or a flush gap.
b: Dogfood finding 2026-08-22: the embedding damage is 475 of 509 concepts, not 92 of 100; the earlier figure is stale and understates the backfill by roughly five times.

a: CORRECTION to the same-day claim that the 512-token clamp was a plausible contributor to the unembedded-concept damage — measured against the live dogfood store 2026-08-22, it is NOT the dominant cause. Coverage is 34 embedded of 509 concepts (93% unembedded), and the gap does not track length: concepts under 400 chars are 2/247 embedded, worse than the 400-1200 band at 32/232, while 1200-2400 is 0/30. Sub-400-char concepts never reach the 512-token clamp, so something else — the originally recorded cause, the embedder unreachable or refusing silently across whole sessions — accounts for the bulk. The clamp is still real and still worth its fix (it hard-fails every long input), but it is a second failure mode, not the explanation. Recency confirms the split: the ten newest concepts are 9/10 embedded (written after the clamp fix, with the embedder up), every earlier 100-row band is 2-8%.
b: The 512-token llama-server clamp is a plausible contributor to the 92 of 100 unembedded dogfood concepts: any input over about 512 tokens fails with HTTP 500 and, on a pre-J3 binary, the write applied with a NULL embedding.

a: The dogfood embedder's capacity flags are LOAD-BEARING, not tuning (found by K1's NVIDIA leg 2026-08-22, reproduced and fixed live on the Mac rig the same day, DOGFOOD-SETUP.md updated). llama-server clamps n_batch = n_ubatch = 512 by default, so ANY input over ~512 tokens fails HTTP 500 'input too large to process' — the J3-R3-1 failure class reachable by plain input length, no network fault needed. BGE-M3 carries 8192-token capacity; the defaults throw away fifteen sixteenths of it. On a pre-J3 binary such a write applied with embedding = NULL while the receipt said 'applied', so this is a plausible contributor to the 92/100 unembedded dogfood concepts. Run with --batch-size 8192 --ubatch-size 8192 -c 8192 (long flags only; this build rejects -u), and verify with a >512-token embed, NOT /health — health passes either way, which is how it hid.
b: The dogfood llama-server's capacity flags are tuning only: the defaults handle every input and only change throughput.

a: J3 round-3 residual handed outside J3, for E2E/J4: a concept applied with a NULL embedding is unfindable by semantic recall, and neither the ack, the receipt, nor a warning says so — the receipt reads 'applied — derived 1 concept(s): 1 created, 0 matched existing' with warnings: []. Pre-existing hybrid-derive degradation, not touched by these commits, but J3 is what made a fast vector-less Ok load-bearing for durability (J3-R3-1). Any E2E durability measurement must therefore assert on the STORE's embedding column, not on applied counts: 'applied' does not mean 'embedded'. Reviewer note for future rounds: read back store state with sqlite3 rather than trusting lambo_stats' applied count, and burst MULTI-AGENT as well as multi-size — round 2's single-agent-only red/green is what let J3-R3-2 through.
b: A concept applied with a NULL embedding is flagged in its receipt as 'applied (unembedded)' and a warning names the failed embed, so the ack alone tells the caller.

a: Claude Code enforcement layer 2026-09-01: instructions alone do not make Claude Code follow the lambo-dogfood protocol (operator observation: other harnesses comply from AGENTS.md text; Claude Code is notorious for skipping it). Fix is mechanical, at user scope so it covers every project: ~/.claude/settings.json hooks driving ~/lambo-dogfood/hooks/lambo-hook.sh. SessionStart injects the protocol + writer health; PreToolUse denies Edit/Write/NotebookEdit until the session has made one lambo_recall (bounded at 2 denials so restricted-toolset agents cannot deadlock); PostToolUse markers track recall/derive/edit per session_id under ~/lambo-dogfood/hooks/state; Stop blocks ending a turn that edited files without a derive or record_action, once per session, honoring stop_hook_active. Every gate fails open when the writer is down. Verified live: a Write was denied, lambo_recall lifted the gate, the retry succeeded.
b: Claude Code follows the lambo-dogfood protocol from AGENTS.md text alone, like the other harnesses, so no hooks are needed.

a: J1 gates everything multi-client: the serve applies its own --agent to every connected client, and lambo_reserve hard-refuses any caller whose agent_id differs — correct fail-closed behaviour that leaves every client but one without lambo's only mutual-exclusion primitive. Per-call agent_id must be accepted at the Memory level and recorded on the interaction before a proxy or shared writer can be honest.
b: lambo_reserve accepts any caller's agent_id as long as the reservation does not overlap another one, so many clients can share one serve without per-call identity.

a: J1 round-2 lesson: matching an error VARIANT is not matching a PATH. conflict_err matched LamboError::Conflict to surface §11 reserve conflicts, but lease_lost_error() is also a Conflict and interpolates OPERATOR_OVERRIDE (a SQL DELETE), so the fix disclosed to the model what the parent had flattened. When selectively unhiding an error class, discriminate structurally (distinct variant or typed payload, or match at the site where sources are distinguishable), never by variant alone — and probe every producer of that variant before shipping.
b: When selectively unhiding an error class to the model, matching on the error variant is enough, because each variant has exactly one producer.

b: The proxy's dial budget is 60 seconds, one lease TTL plus slack.

a: J3 latency claim VERIFIED at the release binary over real stdio MCP (2026-08-20, SQLite store, 20 calls, median): against the rig's live llama.cpp BGE-M3 q8_0 on CPU, a lambo_derive ack went from 14.111 ms (base 166a3c8, synchronous) to 0.048 ms (J3). That 0.048 ms is at or BELOW the same binary's ack against FixtureEmbedder (0.076 ms), which is what 'the embedder is no longer in the call' means. Both runs applied all 21 concepts, so the fast number is not a fast no-op. The absolute figures differ from the doc's 27 ms warm derive because that was the dogfood client stack on pinned 3039b82; the delta is what J3 owns.
b: After J3 a lambo_derive ack still waits for the embedder, so it costs about 14 ms against a CPU llama.cpp BGE-M3.

a: J3 acks a derive once its intent is durable in the write queue, before the embedder runs; the receipt (lambo_receipt) later reports applied, refused or lost, and is the only place a write's real outcome appears.
b: J3 acks a derive only after the concept is applied and embedded, so the ack itself is the outcome and receipts are optional.

a: Workstream B is extract-then-extend, not copy-then-edit: B0 extracts PgStore<D: Dialect> from the hardened Cockroach adapter (move-only commit first, then carve), with postgres and cockroach as dialect files. A function enters the shared base only when its SQL is byte-identical across dialects — never forced together with a bool parameter. Copy-then-edit was rejected: it makes Postgres a second-class citizen and dual maintenance reliably fails (F-R2-2 demonstrated it).
b: Workstream B is copy-then-edit: the Postgres adapter starts as a copy of the Cockroach adapter and the two are edited independently.

a: Alias split: config strings postgres/pg resolve to PgStore<PostgresDialect>, cockroach/crdb to PgStore<CockroachDialect> — nothing maps across the boundary. This is a recorded behaviour change that fails loud, never silently mis-ranks: the Postgres dialect's CREATE EXTENSION vector and <=> operator do not exist on Cockroach, so cross-misconfiguration dies at provision or first vector query.
b: Alias split: the config string postgres resolves to PgStore<CockroachDialect> when the server reports Cockroach, so a crossed config keeps working.

a: Unreleased (#179): any concept that a newer concept contradicts, more recently than anything that supports it, carries the Contradicted warning. Before, against only flagged a Canonical or Venerable concept.

a: Unreleased (#179): an ordinary contradicted hit must earn its own place in the first top_k; when it does, its contradicting concept is added beside it, past top_k if needed, at most one extra hit per contradicted hit, carrying companion_of.
b: Unreleased (#179): a Canonical or Venerable contradicted hit is kept past top_k, and the contradicting concept is shown beside it.

a: Unreleased (#197): GC no longer collects the correction of a contradicted ordinary concept; a sweep protects the correction of every contradiction the detector reports, as long as the contradicted concept is still in memory. Concepts that only contradict each other keep none of themselves alive.
b: 0.6.0: GC protects a concept that contradicts a Venerable or Canonical concept until that target is demoted; contradicting ordinary memory protects nothing.

a: 0.6.0 (#19): against on lambo_derive and lambo_record_action records that a write shows an existing concept to be wrong. A contradiction never changes a score or a status and no longer counts as a GC connection.
b: 0.6.0 (#19): against on lambo_derive lowers the contradicted concept's score by half and demotes it one status.

a: Unreleased (#196): contradictions get a hot-list budget, hot_list_contradiction_max (default half of hot_list_max); over it the lowest-priority contradictions are dropped first, and a full budget keeps the most recently declared ones.
b: Unreleased (#196): contradictions get a hot-list budget equal to hot_list_max, and a full budget keeps the oldest declared contradictions.

a: 0.6.0 (#20): with canonization_supersede = true (off by default), a contradicting concept that earns its own newer evidence demotes the Canonical concept it contradicts, and the audit records why.
b: Supersession is on by default: any contradiction of a Canonical concept demotes it immediately.

a: The recall-twice protocol: recall the topic before reading code, then a targeted recall on the real names afterwards. It came from the J0 arithmetic-deviation reasoning (accepted − written − write_failed), which was in the graph all along but only findable once the reader knew the key name.

a: The 2026-08-27 fair test is precision and recall against ground truth named before the fact: do the four canon-shaped invariants promote while the other ~96 concepts do not. Either direction failing is a finding.
b: The 2026-08-27 fair test passes if any concept promotes within a week of distinct per-call ids.

a: Ground truth for the fair test, the four canon-shaped invariants: (1) the lease stays, a proxy moves the call not the write; (2) the wedge invariant, never acquire a lease you cannot serve; (3) the cooperative-identity ruling; (4) the async-ack rule, a write may be acked asynchronously only when its result does not gate the caller's next action.
b: The async-ack rule: every write is acknowledged asynchronously, including those whose result gates the caller's next action.

a: Blast radius cannot fire on concepts nobody linked: the orchestrator's derives are mostly free-floating prose with almost no parent_of pairs, so 'nothing is load-bearing' is partly a statement about how agents write; nothing on the write surface nudges a caller to declare what a constraint supports.
b: Canonization had never completed on the dogfood store: 0 of 386 concepts carried a stored blast_radius after thousands of daemon cycles.
